questions.q: Which AI use case would make a difference this year, and what stops it from running on your own data today?
questions.why: Anchors the platform in a real use case, not a lab.
questions.need: One use case with a business owner and a measure of success is chosen
questions.how: Pick the use case with the owner and agree how success is measured
questions.listen: One named use case with an owner and a deadline is a project; a list of ideas is not yet.
questions.probe: What happens to that use case if it waits another year?

questions.q: Why does this need to run on your infrastructure: data sensitivity, sovereignty, cost, or latency?
questions.why: The reason decides the architecture and the proof.
questions.need: The reason to run AI in house is written down and agreed
questions.how: Write the reason with the sponsor: data, sovereignty, cost or latency
questions.listen: Sensitivity and sovereignty are lasting reasons; cost alone can change with the next price list.
questions.probe: Which data could never be sent to a hosted model, and who decided?

questions.q: How many GPU servers exist today, who bought them, and how busy are they?
questions.why: Scattered GPUs are expensive and invisible.
questions.need: Every GPU server is known, with an owner and its utilisation
questions.how: List GPU servers and measure a week of utilisation
questions.listen: Idle or scattered GPUs are capacity to pool before buying more.
questions.probe: How busy were the GPUs last month, on average and at peak?

questions.q: Which models are in use, and who approved them?
questions.why: An approved catalogue is the start of governance.
questions.need: The models in use are known and approved
questions.how: Build a catalogue of approved models with an owner
questions.listen: Models in use without approval are a governance gap.
questions.probe: Who checks a model's licence and origin before it is used?

questions.q: Can an assistant reach documents a user is not allowed to read?
questions.why: Permission-aware retrieval is where AI meets data protection.
questions.need: Retrieval respects the same permissions as the source data
questions.how: Test retrieval as two users with different rights
questions.listen: Retrieval that ignores permissions leaks data: it must act with the user's own rights.
questions.probe: How do document permissions reach the assistant today?

questions.q: Are prompts and responses kept where security can investigate them?
questions.why: Without logs, an incident cannot be reconstructed.
questions.need: Prompts and responses are logged and searchable, with agreed retention
questions.how: Turn on logging for the first endpoint and agree retention
questions.listen: Without logs, misuse cannot be investigated.
questions.probe: How long must logs be kept, and who may read them?

questions.q: What may an agent call or change, and who decided?
questions.why: Agents act; their limits must be explicit.
questions.need: Each agent has an owner and a policy on what it may call and change
questions.how: Write the policy for the first agent and enforce it
questions.listen: Agents that can act need the same controls as people.
questions.probe: Which action would you never let an agent take without a person approving it?

questions.q: Who sees what AI costs each team, and decides when it grows?
questions.why: Cost without an owner grows unchecked.
questions.need: AI usage and cost per team are reviewed by a named owner
questions.how: Meter usage per team and review it monthly
questions.listen: Without cost per team, GPU capacity goes to whoever asks first.
questions.probe: Who decides when to buy more GPUs?

questions.q: Which parts of the business already use generative AI, through which services, and with which data?
questions.why: Shadow AI is the first estate to bring under governance.
questions.need: AI use across the business is known: who uses which models and services, with which data
questions.how: Survey teams and network logs for AI services already in use
questions.listen: Use through public services shows the demand and the risk at once.
questions.probe: Which of these services hold company data today?

questions.q: Who owns AI in the business, and is the programme followed by the board?
questions.why: The owner of the AI programme decides what gets built and funded; infrastructure follows.
questions.need: The AI programme has a named owner, goals the board follows, and a seat for infrastructure
questions.how: Find out who sponsors AI and bring them a concrete use case
questions.listen: Board attention brings budget and deadlines.
questions.probe: What did the board ask for at its last review?

questions.q: Is AI cost measured per finished piece of work rather than per token, and could the model behind an application be swapped without code changes?
questions.why: Cheaper tokens can still make a dearer result if a model needs many more of them; and a model wired into code cannot follow better offers.
questions.need: Each use case has a known cost per finished piece of work, and applications reach models through one shared endpoint, so the model can change
questions.how: Cost one use case end to end on two models, and put a shared endpoint between applications and models
questions.listen: Cost per finished task is how the business will judge it.
questions.probe: Which task would you measure first, and what does it cost today by hand?

questions.q: Where do your models run today (a hosted service, a public cloud, a GPU cloud, your own data centre), and how is each paid for?
questions.why: Each place is billed differently: per token, per hour, or owned; the mix decides the cost.
questions.need: Every place models run is known, with how it is billed
questions.how: List each model in use, where it runs and how it is paid for
questions.listen: Several places with several sets of controls is the sprawl to bring together.
questions.probe: Which of these would you bring in-house first, and why?

questions.q: Which AI work is at which stage: answers from your documents, coding assistants, applications with agents, agents that run on their own?
questions.why: Each stage needs more control than the last; where each team is says what to build first.
questions.need: Each AI initiative is placed at its stage, with the controls that stage needs
questions.how: Place each initiative at its stage, with its owner
questions.listen: Most work starts with answers from documents; agents raise the bar on control.
questions.probe: Which application is closest to production?

questions.q: How will GPUs be shared between teams, with limits, isolation and usage per team?
questions.why: Scarce GPUs without quotas go to whoever asks first, and nobody can see who uses what.
questions.need: GPUs are shared with quotas, isolation and metering per team
questions.how: Agree quotas per team and turn on usage metering
questions.listen: Sharing with limits and isolation lets more teams use fewer GPUs.
questions.probe: How is a GPU given to a team today, and how long does it take?

questions.q: Must any of it run disconnected from the internet, or to a hardening standard?
questions.why: Air-gapped and hardened deployments change how models, updates and support reach the platform.
questions.need: Use cases that need an air gap or a hardening standard are known and planned for
questions.how: List the use cases that need an air gap or a hardening standard
questions.listen: Running disconnected changes how models and updates are delivered.
questions.probe: How are software updates brought into the isolated network today?

questions.q: How much new data will each AI pipeline create, and where will it live and be protected?
questions.why: Embeddings, checkpoints and logs multiply the data; unplanned, they fill the fastest storage.
questions.need: The data each pipeline creates is sized, placed and protected
questions.how: Estimate the data each pipeline creates and give it a place and a protection policy
questions.listen: Vector indexes, checkpoints and logs grow fast; they need sizing and protection too.
questions.probe: Who protects the data AI creates, and has it ever been restored?

questions.q: For the first use case: what size of model, how many users at once, and what response time is acceptable?
questions.why: Model size, concurrency and response time size the GPUs.
questions.need: Model size, concurrent users and target response time are agreed for the first use case
questions.how: Agree a model class, peak users and a response time with the use case owner
questions.listen: These three numbers size GPU memory and count; without them sizing is a guess.
questions.probe: How long a document or conversation must the model read at once?

questions.q: How will answers be checked for quality and safety, before going live and after?
questions.why: Evaluation decides whether a use case reaches production.
questions.need: Quality and safety checks are agreed for the first use case
questions.how: Agree test questions and pass criteria with the use case owner
questions.listen: A set of test questions with expected answers becomes the proof's success criteria.
questions.probe: Who signs off that the answers are good enough to release?
